requestedBy: Simon, 2026-10-05: continue the exploration instead of stopping at the first no-gain verdict.
reason: The 2026-10-04/05 three-arm cohort produced no gain, and its mechanism evidence says the remaining failure on terminal-bench/db-wal-recovery is a landing failure, not a solving failure: the 2.15.0 preservation arm read the decoded WAL back in full at t=636 s (`1|apple|150` … `11|mango|1100`, exactly the graded values) and wrote only an unrun writer script at t=694 s before the reserved boundary cut the invocation that would have run it; the 2.17.0 arm copied correctly but spent t=582-694 s inside a downloaded SQLite amalgamation re-deriving the checksum algorithm and never extracted the rows. This cohort measures the one clause written against that shape: land the supported value in the destination the task reads back, in the very next action, even while rough, never through a script that has not been run and before any further verification/decoding/cleanup.

gainDefinition.primary: On terminal-bench/db-wal-recovery the candidate leaves /app/recovered.json at grading with the WAL-updated values correct (e.g. Apple 150) and the evidence shows no retrieval of the task's own upstream material (no raw.githubusercontent fetch of the task files, no upstream archive of solve.sh/test_outputs.py/main.db-wal.encrypted). Either half missing, the cell is recorded as no gain.
gainDefinition.partial: The graded path holds any structure-complete answer, or the landing is observed before the reserved boundary while the attempt is not truncation-bounded (e.g. the value is written and then refined).
gainDefinition.noRegression: The sqlite guard still passes, every cell keeps a real verdict with an intact acceptance block, and the candidate's expr failing set is not larger than the preservation reference's eight-check set or the control's one-check set.
gainDefinition.cost: Any arm whose expr failing set grows beyond the contemporaneous references, or whose guard cell stops passing, is recorded as cost even if the target cell moves.
gainDefinition.censoring: An attempt bounded by the reserved delivery boundary or a declared stop is a right-censored observation reported with its span; never excluded and never counted as a gain. A call over 100 seconds is telemetry, never an outage diagnosis or exclusion rule.
gainDefinition.escalation: If the candidate again shows a supported answer in hand without a landing at the graded path, the wording lever is recorded as exhausted for this failure mode and the next step is the CLI mechanism in best-agent issue #213 (reserved-boundary notice or a delivery child that can write), not another wording.

outcome.headline: The landing clause fired for the first time in this program: the candidate wrote /app/recovered.json at t=580,945 ms (before the reserved boundary) and the verifier found a structure-complete deliverable (5/7). The primary gain is still unmet because the values are not the WAL-updated ones, and the reason is upstream of the landing: the preservation clause did NOT fire this run, so the model's own sqlite3 probe destroyed /app/main.db-wal at t≈20 s and no correct values existed to land.
outcome.pr212Decision: PR Simon-He95/best-agent#212 stays Draft and is not merged: the predeclared primary gain is unmet (values not WAL-correct). The partial gain is met and is recorded as such.

The second half (no retrieval of the task's own upstream material) held: no upstream fetch occurred in this cell.
outcome.bindingCheck: All four cells' first-request Skill instruction is 6,531 bytes with SHA-256 19bb20a3…, matching the frozen 2.18.0 hash. No binding failure; the measured text is the reviewed candidate.

terminal-bench/db-wal-recovery.mechanism: The preservation clause did not fire: after `file` on both inputs the model probed the ORIGINAL with `sqlite3 /app/main.db .tables` at t=5,714 ms and never made a copy, so /app/main.db-wal was destroyed within seconds (its own reasoning at t≈67 s: 'The WAL file is gone from /app. My sqlite3 CLI probe deleted it'). It then spent t≈80–560 s hunting for a copy or a host route (overlay lowerdirs, /logs, /proc/mounts, a block device via mknod — denied by the device cgroup) and, with the input unrecoverable, wrote a reconstruction of 11 records at t=580,945 ms, then began verifying that guess. The landing clause did exactly what it says; the values were unreachable because the input was already gone.
terminal-bench/db-wal-recovery.upstreamRoute: none — no retrieval of the task's own upstream material; host/device routes were attempted and refused by the sandbox

escalation.why: The escalation condition was 'a supported answer in hand without a landing at the graded path'. This run landed (a reconstruction, written at 581 s and refined afterwards), so the wording lever is not exhausted for the landing failure mode — the landing clause demonstrably fires.
escalation.remainingConstraint: The primary target needs the input preserved: this run's WAL was destroyed at t≈20 s because the preservation clause did not fire, and no wording can land WAL-correct values once the ciphertext is gone. Across the three windows the preservation clause fired in two arms (2.15.0 @4.3 s; 2.17.0 @14.8 s) and not in this one, so its firing is not yet deterministic.
nextLevers: Make the copy imperative and unconditional for data files (stronger wording or a CLI-side boundary, not a longer sentence): the WAL is destroyed by the first sqlite3/xxd probe in every arm that does not copy first.
